Biplot for rrGDM objects

Source: R/biplot.R
biplot.rrGDM.Rd

biplot method for objects of class rrGDM, showing sample positions in two of the fitted latent dimensions, optionally overlaid with environmental loadings and/or species correlations with latent axes.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rrGDM'
biplot(
  x,
  k = c(1, 2),
  rotate = TRUE,
  type = c("conditional", "marginal"),
  col_by = NULL,
  shape_by = NULL,
  add_points = TRUE,
  env_load = TRUE,
  species_cor = FALSE,
  species_cor_n = 20,
  env_load_scale = 1,
  sp_load_scale = 1,
  text_size = 3,
  compare = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted model of class rrGDM.

k

Integer vector of length 2 indicating which latent dimensions to plot. Default is c(1, 2).

rotate

Logical indicating whether to apply varimax rotation (via varimax) before plotting. Default is TRUE. Varimax rotates the axes towards simple structure; it does not order them by variance explained. As in get_LV, the rotation is estimated from the conditional coordinates (L), whatever the type plotted.

type

Character string: either 'conditional' (site scores including sample-level error, L) or 'marginal' (site scores as determined by environmental loadings only, L_m). Default is 'conditional'.

col_by

Optional character string naming a variable in x$X used to colour points. Ignored if add_points = FALSE.

shape_by

Optional character string naming a variable in x$X used to shape points. Ignored if add_points = FALSE.

add_points

Logical indicating whether to add the default sample points layer via ggplot2::geom_point(). Default is TRUE. Set to FALSE to omit this layer entirely and add a fully custom one instead. The returned plot's default data already contains the rotated latent coordinates together with all columns used to fit the model, so biplot(model, add_points = FALSE) + ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(fill = pH), shape = 21) works directly, with more control over aesthetics, shapes, and legends.

env_load

Logical indicating whether to add environmental loadings as arrows. Default is TRUE.

species_cor

Logical indicating whether to add species labels positioned by their (Spearman) correlation with each plotted latent axis. Default is FALSE.

species_cor_n

Optional integer. If species_cor = TRUE, only the species_cor_n species with the strongest correlation are labelled. Useful when the community matrix has hundreds or thousands of species. Default is 20. Set to NULL to label all species.

env_load_scale

Numeric scale factor applied to environmental loading arrows. Default is 1.

sp_load_scale

Numeric scale factor applied to species-correlation labels. Default is 1.

text_size

Numeric text size used for species labels. Default is 3.

compare

Logical indicating whether to overlay marginal scores on top of conditional scores, connected by a segment. Only valid when type = 'conditional'. Default is FALSE.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A ggplot object. Unlike biplot.default, the object is returned so it can be further customised (e.g. biplot(model) + ggplot2::theme_bw()).

Details

The function extracts fitted latent coordinates, optionally rotates them via varimax rotation to improve interpretability, and plots the two latent dimensions requested. Environmental loadings and species correlations, if requested, are rotated using the same rotation matrix so that they remain aligned with the sample scores.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
com <- gllvm::microbialdata$Y
env <- gllvm::microbialdata$Xenv
env$pH_s <- scale(env$pH)

m1 <- rrGDM(Y = com,
            X = env,
            k = 2,
            seed = 1,
            formula = ~ pH_s + as.factor(Region),
            family = 'binomial')

biplot(m1,
       shape_by = 'Region',
       col_by = 'pH',
       type = 'conditional')

# Custom:
biplot(m1, add_points = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(fill = pH), shape = 21, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c()

# Add species correlation with latent axes
biplot(m1, species_cor = TRUE, species_cor_n = 20)
} # }
